_how_to_read: solids[*].min/max: for a solid that exists in our mesh ('solid' is its index as tools/build_model.py numbers connected components) these are OUR solid's box, and box_error_mm says how far Cadasio's box for the same body is from it (sum of the six face offsets).

solids[*].solid = null: a Cadasio body with no solid of its own in our mesh; min/max are then Cadasio's box moved into our mesh coordinates. 'inside_solid' names our solid whose box contains it (it was welded into that solid, or is a face copy lying on it).

skin = true: in our mesh this solid is an open shell lying within 0.05 mm of another solid (Cadasio name contains 'Surface-Offset'): a coloured face copy. The solid underneath must take the same colour or it shows through.
set_in_step = true: the colour was set in Cadasio (colour_main on the solid or an ancestor). false: Cadasio shows the SolidWorks colour (cad_colour) unchanged.

also_covers: Cadasio bodies of another colour that are part of this one solid in our mesh (they touch, so our split into connected solids cannot separate them). The colour given is that of the body whose box is nearest to the solid's.
shown = false: the author pushed this body under another surface, so it is not seen (servo label only).

Entries copied from the MRA keep the MRA's fields: 'solid' indices are the MRA mesh's numbering (rcc.glb is tessellated more coarsely and numbers some meshes' solids differently; the match is by boxes, so this does not matter), and 'instances' here lists the RCC instances that carry the mesh, with the MRA's in 'mra_instances'.

Entries from the RCC Cadasio ('source': 'rcc_cadasio') are tools/cadasio/atlas.py's output for that component: each solid's Cadasio box (identical to ours in the mesh's own frame, to 0.005 mm) and the colour it shows most often while visible; 'shown' is the number of visible steps.

materials.json may swap an atlas colour for a palette entry (a rule's atlas_colours): the FS90R's colours go through palette names so that one ruling from Lee changes them everywhere, and the lead stubs take the colours of the leads the player draws.
_about: DRAFT for "PMG Build Instructions/colour-atlas-pmg.json": the MRA's colour atlas entries (copied through the RCC's, unchanged) for the parts the PMG shares with the MRA: the I/O module (NAUO78) and the Nano (NANO). The PMG's own parts are coloured by rules (materials.json).
